world-clock.formula:
For each zone Z, every second:
localTime(Z) = Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { timeZone: Z, hour, minute, second })
offset(Z) = minutes where local(Z) = UTC + offset, via formatToParts
isDay = 6 <= localHour(Z) < 18

Your card uses the device timezone directly (no conversion).
howTo: Your own local time ticks at the top for reference.

keyFacts: Every clock is computed from your device's clock plus the browser's timezone database — nothing is fetched from a server.
A timezone offset is not constant: the same city can show UTC+1 in October and UTC+0 in January.
The International Date Line means it can be a different calendar day on opposite sides of the Pacific — each card shows its own date.
The sun/moon icon reflects actual local daytime (6:00–18:00) at that place right now.
All 18 zones update together every second with a single lightweight timer.
